mainTopic: The dispute over how a שומר who misuses a deposit pays, the הלכה about רבי עקיבא, and a new משנה on planning to misuse a deposit and on tilting versus lifting a barrel
overview: The גמרא first decides that בית הלל's 'כשעת הוצאה' means the value at the moment the שומר took the deposit for himself. That seems to put רבה on the side of בית שמאי. To avoid this, the גמרא tries three explanations of the dispute. The first is whether שליחות יד needs actual loss. The second is whether a שואל שלא מדעת counts as a thief. Each of these would make רבא follow בית שמאי, so the גמרא settles on a third: the schools argue about שבח גזילה, such as wool and newborn young, the same argument as רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. The wording of the משנה supports this. Next the גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא, who sets the value at the time of the claim. שמואל rules like him, and there is a debate over whether witnesses change his rule. רבי יוחנן says the הלכה is 'always' like רבי עקיבא, and רב אשי explains what 'always' adds, while רבא rules like בית הלל. A new משנה then asks whether merely planning to misuse a deposit creates liability. It also contrasts tilting a barrel with lifting it.

steps.title: Removal means taking it out of the owner's house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that בית הלל's phrase 'כשעת הוצאה' means the moment the deposit was taken out of the owner's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that 'the time of removal' means the time it was taken out of the owner's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the earlier question about what 'removal' means in בית הלל's view. The answer: the moment the שומר took the item away for his own use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two ways to read 'הוצאה': removal from the world (when the item was destroyed), or removal from the owner's house (when it was misused). The גמרא decides it must be the second. So according to בית הלל, the שומר pays based on the item's value at the moment he misused it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Removal, taking out
The owner's house (the owner's domain)
Rather (rejects the other option)

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious
that it is according to the time of removal from the owner's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the earlier inquiry (before this section) into the meaning of 'כשעת הוצאה'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית הלל: the שומר pays according to the value at the moment of misuse, when the item left the owner's house.

steps.title: Does רבה side with בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: If בית הלל fix the value at the time of misuse, then רבה, who has the thief pay the later increased value, seems to follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבה ruled like בית שמאי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's earlier ruling. It now seems to match only the losing view of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה ruled that a thief pays the higher value at the time he broke the item. בית הלל now seem to fix the payment at the moment of misuse. That would mean רבה goes against בית הלל, and the הלכה normally follows בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggested problem)
The school of שמאי

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rabba
said his ruling like Beit Shammai?!
phrases.notes: רבה had ruled that a thief who breaks the item pays its higher, later value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a troubling consequence from the conclusion in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that a thief pays the increased value at the time of breaking
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בית הלל fix the value at the moment of misuse, then charging the later increased value matches only בית שמאי.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about an increase in value
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that בית שמאי and בית הלל agree when the value goes up. They argue only when it goes down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה can tell you: about an increase in value, everyone agrees. They argue only about a decrease.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by narrowing the dispute. It now covers only a case where the item lost value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the item went up in value, even בית הלל agree that he pays the higher value at the time of breaking. That fits רבה. The argument between the schools is limited to a drop in value.

keyTerms.meaning: He can tell you (a defense on someone's behalf)
Increase (in value)
Decrease (in value)
Everyone

phrases.english: Rabba can say to you:
regarding an increase, everyone does not disagree;
when they disagree, it is about a decrease.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about both an increase and a decrease.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree about an increase, so רבה fits everyone. They argue only about a decrease.

steps.title: Does misusing an item require actual loss?
steps.stepSummary: The argument about a decrease is explained: בית שמאי say שליחות יד does not need actual loss, and בית הלל say it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that misuse does not require loss, so when the item decreases, it decreases in his possession. בית הלל hold that misuse requires loss, so when it decreases, it decreases in the owner's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the argument about a drop in value. This completes רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the mere act of misuse makes the שומר responsible like a thief. Any later drop in value is therefore his loss, and he pays the original higher value. For בית הלל, he becomes liable only once there is real loss. Until then the item is still the owner's, so a drop in value is the owner's loss.

keyTerms.meaning: A שומר using the deposit for himself (misuse)
Loss, physical reduction
In his own possession or responsibility
In its owner's possession

steps.whatToRemember: The first explanation: the argument is whether שליחות יד needs actual loss. That decides whose loss a drop in value is.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
misuse does not require loss;
and when it decreases, it decreases in his possession.
And Beit Hillel hold:
misuse requires loss;
and when it decreases, it decreases in its owner's possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: שְׁלִיחוּת יָד אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה חֶסְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the narrowed dispute in step 3.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute about a decrease depends on whether שליחות יד requires actual loss.

steps.title: Then רבא would side with בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבא ruled that שליחות יד does not require loss. Under step 4, that would be בית שמאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about רבא's statement that misuse does not require loss? Shall we say that רבא ruled like בית שמאי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation in step 4. It makes another אמורא, רבא, follow בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 tied 'no loss needed' to בית שמאי only. Yet רבא rules this way as the accepted הלכה. It is hard to say רבא follows בית שמאי against בית הלל, so the explanation in step 4 cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא רבא (a different sage from רבה)
That which he said

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבה (step 2) and רבא (here). They are two different אמוראים with two different rulings.

phrases.english: But this that Rava said:
misuse does not require loss,
shall we say that Rava said it like Beit Shammai?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the schools argue about whether שליחות יד requires loss
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That explanation puts רבא's ruling in line with בית שמאי against בית הלל, which is unacceptable.

steps.title: A new setting: borrowing the barrel to reach birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reframes the case. The שומר moved the barrel to stand on it and reach young birds. The real dispute is about borrowing without the owner's knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with? Where he moved the barrel to stand on it and bring down young birds. They argue about one who borrows without the owner's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the explanation from step 4 and gives a new case. It also names a new topic of dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing on a barrel is not taking it for keeps. It is like borrowing it briefly without permission. So the dispute is no longer about whether שליחות יד needs loss, and רבא's ruling is free to fit everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
He moved it
Young birds, fledglings
One who borrows without the owner's knowledge

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
For example, where he moved it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the barrel being looked after.

phrases.english: to bring young birds by standing upon it,
and they disagree about one who borrows without the owner's knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by replacing the explanation of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The schools argue about whether שליחות יד requires loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about the status of a שואל שלא מדעת, so רבא's ruling fits everyone.

steps.title: Is an unauthorized borrower a thief or a borrower?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי treat a שואל שלא מדעת as a thief, so a drop in value is his loss. בית הלל treat him as a borrower, so a drop in value is the owner's loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that one who borrows without knowledge is a thief, so when the item decreases, it decreases in his possession. בית הלל hold that he is a borrower, so when it decreases, it decreases in the owner's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both sides of the new dispute about borrowing without permission. This finishes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, moving the barrel without permission makes him a גזלן right away. He then bears any drop in value and pays the original price. For בית הלל, he is only a borrower, so the barrel stays in the owner's possession until it breaks. He pays its value at the time it was damaged.

keyTerms.meaning: A robber, one who takes by force
A borrower
Is considered

steps.whatToRemember: The second explanation: the schools argue about whether a שואל שלא מדעת counts as a גזלן or a שואל. This frees רבא's ruling that שליחות יד needs no loss, but the next step challenges this explanation too.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that unauthorized borrowing is its own category. Whether such a borrower counts as a thief or a borrower decides who bears a drop in value.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
one who borrows without the owner's knowledge is a robber;
and when it decreases, it decreases in his possession.
And Beit Hillel hold:
one who borrows without the owner's knowledge is a borrower;
and when it decreases, it decreases in its owner's possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: שׁוֹאֵל שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת גַּזְלָן הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two positions in the new dispute named in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the underlying principle of the new framing
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי: a שואל שלא מדעת is a גזלן and bears the decrease. בית הלל: he is a שואל, so the owner bears the decrease.

steps.title: Would רבא Be Following בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks step 7. רבא said that according to the רבנן, a שואל שלא מדעת is a גזלן. If that is בית שמאי's view, רבא would be siding with בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about רבא, who said: someone who borrows without the owner knowing is a robber according to the רבנן? Should we say that רבא ruled like בית שמאי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 7. If 'a שואל שלא מדעת is a thief' is בית שמאי's view, then רבא's ruling would follow בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We normally do not rule like בית שמאי against בית הלל. Yet רבא stated his rule as the view of the רבנן, the mainstream position. So the explanation in step 7 cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: a robber; someone who takes property by force or without permission
according to the רבנן (the Sages, the majority view)
shall we say? (usually brings an idea the גמרא does not want to accept)

phrases.english: But this that Rava said:
one who borrows without the owner's knowledge –
according to the Rabbis, he is a robber,
shall we say that Rava ruled like Beit Shammai?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that בית שמאי treat a שואל שלא מדעת as a thief.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא gives that rule as the רבנן's view. If it belonged to בית שמאי, רבא would be following a view we do not rule like.

steps.title: The Argument Is About Improvement of Stolen Property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation. 'Decrease and increase' means physical changes to the animal, like shearing and giving birth. בית שמאי say the improvement goes to the owner, and בית הלל say it goes to the robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they argue about the improvement of stolen property. בית שמאי hold that the improvement belongs to the victim. בית הלל hold that the improvement belongs to the robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier explanations. It now says the argument is about who keeps the added value of a stolen item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Decrease' now means the animal lost value because it was sheared, and 'increase' means it gained value by giving birth. בית שמאי make the robber pay for everything, including the improvement. בית הלל say the improvement is his, so he pays only what the item was worth when he took it.

keyTerms.meaning: the improvement or added value of stolen property
the one who was robbed; the victim
they argue about

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about prices going up or down in the market. It is about real physical changes to the animal: wool and newborn young.

phrases.english: Rather, here
they argue about the improvement of stolen property.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
the improvement of stolen property belongs to the one robbed,
and Beit Hillel hold:
the improvement of stolen property belongs to the robber.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא בְּשֶׁבַח שֶׁל גְּזֵילָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8 by explaining the dispute in a completely new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: 'decrease and increase' means physical changes, not changes in market value.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about borrowing without permission while market prices changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about who owns the improvement of stolen property, so רבא is not tied to בית שמאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: שבח גזילה (who owns the improvement of stolen property) is a major topic in the laws of robbery.

steps.title: The Same Dispute Between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links this to a ברייתא. A robber stole a ewe, and it was sheared or gave birth. רבי מאיר says he pays for the ewe, the wool, and the young. רבי יהודה says the ewe itself is returned as it is now.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they argue about the same thing as these תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: someone who steals a ewe, and he sheared it or it gave birth, pays for it, its wool, and its young. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the stolen item is returned as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל matches an argument between other תנאים. This helps explain the dispute; it is not an attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes the robber pay for the improvements too, the same as בית שמאי. רבי יהודה says only the ewe goes back and the robber keeps the improvements, the same as בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: a dispute
תנאים, the Sages of the משנה era
its shorn wool
its young (its offspring)
is returned as it is

phrases.english: And they argue about the dispute of these tanna'im,
as it is taught: one who robs a ewe,
and he sheared it or it gave birth,

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁלֵּם אוֹתָהּ וְאֶת גִּיזּוֹתֶיהָ וְאֶת וַלְדוֹתֶיהָ,
phrases.english: pays for it and for its wool and for its young,
this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
The stolen item is returned as it is.
phrases.notes: He means only the ewe goes back in its current state. The robber does not pay extra for the wool or the young.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the new explanation from step 9 matches a known argument in a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר makes the robber pay for the improvements, and רבי יהודה returns only the item itself. This matches בית שמאי and בית הלל.

steps.title: The Wording of the משנה Supports This
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves its explanation from the משנה's words. בית שמאי say 'חסר ויתר', which means something physically missing or added. That fits wool and young.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, since it teaches: בית שמאי say he is penalized for what is lacking and what is added. בית הלל say he pays by the time he took it out. Learn from this that the explanation is correct.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its new explanation from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not use words about prices going up or down. 'Lacking' and 'added' describe something physically removed or added to the animal, like shorn wool or a newborn. So the dispute really is about שבח גזילה.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also exact (it supports this reading)
he is penalized; he must bear the cost
what is lacking and what is added
the time he took the item out for his own use
learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: In the final reading, the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל is about who keeps the physical improvements, like wool and young, of an item the שומר misused.

phrases.english: The wording is also exact, as it teaches:
Beit Shammai say
he is penalized for what is lacking and what is added,
and Beit Hillel say:
according to the time he took it out.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds proof for the explanation in step 9 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute is about physical improvement (שבח גזילה), not changes in market price.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'ילקה בחסר וביתר', words that describe physical loss and gain.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: Value at the Time of the Claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא from the משנה: the payment is set by the item's value at the time of the claim. שמואל rules like רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: he pays by the value at the time of the claim. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the third opinion in the משנה, רבי עקיבא's, and gives the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not look at the time of the misuse. He looks at the time the owner makes his claim in court. שמואל rules that this is the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: the time of the claim in court
the practical law follows (this opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical ruling for when the שומר's payment is calculated.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: according to the time of the claim.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from בית שמאי and בית הלל to the next opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment is set by the item's value at the time of the claim, and the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא Agrees When There Are Witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא agrees that when there are עדים to the misuse, the value is set at that moment, not at the time of the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא agrees in a case where there are witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, still speaking in the name of שמואל, adds an exception to רבי עקיבא's rule: a case with עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule stays 'time of the claim'. But if עדים saw the misuse, רבי עקיבא agrees the payment follows the time of the misuse. The גמרא will give the reason next.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees (admits a point)
witnesses

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva agrees
in a case where there are witnesses.
phrases.notes: He means witnesses who saw the שומר misuse the item. Then the value is set from that moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי עקיבא's rule from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there are עדים to the misuse, even רבי עקיבא sets the value at the time of the misuse.

steps.title: What Is the Reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why witnesses make a difference for רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source and logic behind the exception. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is why the presence of עדים moves the payment date from the claim back to the moment of the misuse.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the exception in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why עדים make the value be set at the time of the misuse, according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Paying From the Day He Became Guilty
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says to pay 'on the day of his guilt'. With עדים, he became guilty at the moment of the misuse, so the value is set from then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: 'To the one it belongs to, he shall give it on the day of his guilt.' Since there are witnesses, from that moment he owes him for his guilt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: payment is set by the day the person becomes guilty. With עדים, that day is the day of the misuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'ביום אשמתו', the day of his guilt. When עדים saw the misuse, his guilt was set right then. That is why רבי עקיבא agrees the value is set at that moment.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק (verse)
on the day of his guilt
guilt; a payment obligation that comes from wrongdoing

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, רבי עקיבא sets the value at the time of the claim. If עדים saw the misuse, the value is set from that moment, because the פסוק says 'ביום אשמתו'. The next step brings רבי יוחנן's tradition, which disagrees.

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"To the one it belongs to, he shall give it
on the day of his guilt,"
and since there are witnesses,
from that moment –
he became liable to him for guilt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא לַאֲשֶׁר הוּא לוֹ יִתְּנֶנּוּ בְּיוֹם אַשְׁמָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ties payment to 'the day of his guilt'. With עדים, his guilt begins at the moment of the misuse.

steps.title: רב אושעיא challenges: רבי עקיבא disagrees even with witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא challenges רב יהודה's claim from step 13. Quoting רבי יוחנן, he says רבי עקיבא disagrees even when there are עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said to רב יהודה: My teacher, you say that? רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי עקיבא disagreed even where there are witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: A student pushes back on what was just said in step 13. He quotes a tradition from רבי יוחנן that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that with עדים, even רבי עקיבא sets the value at the moment of misuse. רבי יוחנן's tradition says no: for רבי עקיבא the value is always set at the time of the claim, even with witnesses. This directly contradicts the earlier statement.

keyTerms.meaning: disagrees, holds a different view
in a case where there are witnesses
'Do you say so?', an expression of surprise and challenge

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said to Rav Yehuda:
My teacher, is that what you say?

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Rabbi Akiva disagreed
even where there are witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from steps 13 to 15 that witnesses change רבי עקיבא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that רבי עקיבא agrees when there are עדים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tradition from רבי יוחנן says רבי עקיבא disagrees even with witnesses, so the earlier claim cannot be right.

steps.title: Why do witnesses not help?
steps.stepSummary: Inside רבי יוחנן's statement, the question is asked: what is the reason?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks why רבי עקיבא would ignore the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 used the same פסוק to show that witnesses do matter. So it is surprising that רבי עקיבא would still wait for the claim, and a reason is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's version of רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי עקיבא sets the value at the claim even when there are עדים.

steps.title: Only the court makes him guilty
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'on the day of his guilt'. Only the בית דין makes a person guilty, not the witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says: 'To the one it belongs to he shall give it on the day of his guilt.' It is the court that makes him guilty.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer reads the same פסוק from step 15 in a different way. 'His guilt' starts only when the בית דין rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, 'the day of his guilt' was the moment the witnesses saw the misuse. Here it means the day the בית דין makes him pay. Witnesses only report what happened; the court is what makes him liable. So the value is always set at the court stage.

keyTerms.meaning: on the day of his guilt
the court
make liable, obligate

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides read 'ביום אשמתו'. One side says guilt begins when the witnesses see the misuse. רבי יוחנן's version says guilt begins only when the בית דין rules.

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"To the one it belongs to he shall give it on the day of his guilt,"
and it is the court
that makes him liable for his guilt.
phrases.notes: The witnesses alone do not make him guilty. Only the court's ruling does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by reading the פסוק from step 15 differently.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אשמתו' happens through the בית דין, so the value is set at the claim even when there are witnesses.

steps.title: רבי זירא sends a student to ask about the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי אבא בר פפא to visit רבי יעקב בר אידי in ארץ ישראל. He should ask whether רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אבא בר פפא: When you go there, take the route around the Ladder of Tyre and go in to רבי יעקב בר אידי. Ask him if he heard from רבי יוחנן whether the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from 'what does רבי עקיבא hold' to 'is the הלכה like him'. This step sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know רבי עקיבא's view, the practical question is whether we follow it. רבי זירא wants a direct tradition from רבי יוחנן, so he sends someone to a student who heard him.

keyTerms.meaning: go around, take a roundabout route
the Ladder of Tyre, a place on the route
did he hear (a tradition)
the law follows the opinion of

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abba bar Pappa:
When you go there,
take the route around the Ladder of Tyre,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי,
phrases.english: and go in to Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi,
and ask him
whether he heard from Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Is the halakha like Rabbi Akiva
or is the halakha not like Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְעִי מִינֵּיהּ אִי שְׁמִיעָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי עקיבא's view to asking about the practical הלכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the הלכה is always like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי answers that רבי יוחנן said: 'הלכה כרבי עקיבא לעולם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה is like רבי עקיבא always.
steps.whatsHappening: The question gets its answer: we follow רבי עקיבא. The extra word 'always' will be explained next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן could have just said 'הלכה כרבי עקיבא'. Adding 'לעולם' hints that some case might have seemed like an exception, and he is saying there is none.

keyTerms.meaning: always, in every case

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha is always like Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question.

steps.title: What does 'always' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'לעולם' comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'always' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking about the extra word 'לעולם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word must teach something. The גמרא wants to know which possible exception 'always' rules out.

keyTerms.meaning: what does 'always' come to add?

phrases.english: What does 'always' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: Always means: even when there are witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that 'always' includes the case with עדים. We follow רבי עקיבא there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: So that you should not say this applies only where there are no witnesses, but not where there are witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that 'always' rules out an exception for cases with witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think we follow רבי עקיבא only without witnesses, as step 13 suggested. 'Always' tells us that even with עדים, the value is set at the time of the claim. This matches רבי יוחנן's tradition in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: so that you should not say
these words apply (only to)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
So that you should not say:
This applies only where there are no witnesses,
but where there are witnesses, it does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאמַר הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by tying 'always' to the witnesses debate.

steps.title: Another meaning: the owner must know the item was returned
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: 'always' includes the case where he put the barrel back and it broke. This rejects רבי ישמעאל, who says the owner does not need to know.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: where he put it back in its place and it broke. This comes to reject רבי ישמעאל, who says the owners do not need to know. It teaches us that the owners do need to know.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second possible explanation of 'always'. It points to an earlier case about returning a misused item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, a person took the barrel, put it back, and then it broke. רבי עקיבא says he is still responsible, because the owner did not know it was returned. רבי ישמעאל says the owner's knowledge is not needed. 'Always' tells us to follow רבי עקיבא in this case too.

keyTerms.meaning: or alternatively
he returned it to its place
the owner's knowledge
to exclude, to reject

steps.confusionAlert: This second explanation is about a different case: returning the item without the owner knowing. It is not about witnesses or when the value is set.

phrases.english: Or alternatively,
where he returned it to its place and it broke,
to reject the view of Rabbi Yishmael,
who says: we do not need the owners' knowledge.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּבָעֵינַן דַּעַת בְּעָלִים.
phrases.english: It teaches us that we do need the owners' knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אשי's answer to step 21 with a second possible meaning of 'לעולם' ('ואי נמי').
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Always' includes the case of returning the item without the owner knowing. The owner's knowledge is required, as רבי עקיבא holds and against רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: רבא: the הלכה follows בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי יוחנן and rules like בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: the הלכה is like בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different final ruling. He follows בית הלל, not רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל in the משנה set the value at the time of the misuse, not at the time of the claim. So רבא's ruling goes against רבי יוחנן's 'הלכה כרבי עקיבא לעולם'.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of הלל

steps.whatToRemember: There are two rulings. רבי יוחנן says the הלכה is always like רבי עקיבא. רבא says the הלכה is like בית הלל.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The halakha is like Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a ruling that competes with רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows בית הלל: the value is set at the time of the misuse.

steps.title: Is planning to misuse a deposit enough to make him liable?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a dispute. בית שמאי say a שומר who plans to misuse a פקדון is already liable. בית הלל say he is liable only once he actually misuses it, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone is watching an item for another person and decides to use it for himself. בית שמאי say he is already responsible for it. בית הלל say he is not responsible until he actually puts his hand on it and uses it, because the תורה says: "if he did not put his hand to his neighbor's goods."
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks whether a שומר becomes liable just by planning to misuse the item he is watching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי treat the plan itself as enough to make the שומר fully responsible for the item. בית הלל say a thought alone does nothing. The פסוק speaks of "putting his hand," so there must be a real action.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: 'our משנה.' It marks the start of a new משנה.
Literally 'sending a hand.' A שומר using the item he is guarding for himself.
A deposit: an item left with someone for safekeeping
One who thinks about or plans something
The two great schools of תנאים who often disagree

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is the base for the whole idea of שליחות יד. It tells us what turns a שומר into someone fully responsible for the item.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who intends to misappropriate a deposit
phrases.notes: Literally 'to send a hand' into the deposit. It means using it for himself.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: he is liable
And Beit Hillel say: he is not liable
until he actually misappropriates it
as it is stated:
"Whether he has not put his hand to his neighbor's goods"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion (Step 24).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: planning to misuse a פקדון already makes the שומר liable. בית הלל: he is liable only after an actual act of misuse, as shown by the פסוק 'שלח ידו'.

steps.title: Tilting the barrel versus lifting it
steps.stepSummary: If the שומר tilts the barrel, takes a רביעית, and the barrel breaks, he pays only for the רביעית. If he lifts the barrel to take the רביעית and it breaks, he pays for the whole barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he tipped the barrel, poured out a רביעית of wine, and then the barrel broke, he pays only for that רביעית. If he picked the barrel up, took a רביעית from it, and then it broke, he pays for the entire barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives two cases of real misuse. It shows that how he took the wine changes how much he must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he only tilts the barrel, he took control of just the wine he poured out. So he pays only for that רביעית. When he lifts the barrel, the lifting counts as taking the whole barrel (הגבהה), so the whole barrel is now his responsibility, even though he drank only a little.

keyTerms.meaning: He tilted or tipped (the barrel) without lifting it
He lifted it up. Lifting is a way of taking possession (הַגְבָּהָה).
A quarter of a לוֹג, a small amount of liquid
A barrel or large jug, here full of wine
The value of the whole (barrel)

steps.confusionAlert: He took the same amount of wine in both cases. The difference is not how much he took but how he handled the barrel: tilting it versus lifting it.
steps.whatToRemember: Thinking alone does not make a שומר liable according to בית הלל. Once he acts, the kind of action matters. Tilting makes him pay only for what he took. Lifting makes him pay for the whole barrel.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two cases become the base for the גמרא's discussion of how far the שומר's liability reaches after שליחות יד.

phrases.english: If he tilted the barrel
and took a quarter-log from it, and it broke
he pays only for the quarter-log
If he lifted it and took a quarter-log from it
and it broke
he pays the value of the whole barrel

steps.triggerLanguage: הִטָּה אֶת הֶחָבִית וְנָטַל הֵימֶנָּה רְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה. After the dispute about mere thought, it shows how an actual act of misuse decides the amount of payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he tilted the barrel and took a רביעית, he pays only for the רביעית. If he lifted the barrel and took a רביעית, he pays for the whole barrel.
